lifecycle.description: The process that is this entity's lifecycle.

rationale.description: Markdown text: why the element is shaped this way.

decision.description: A URL or a reference (such as ADR-0042) of the decision record. It is not an element id and is not checked.

excludeStereotypes.description: Stereotype keys that a database schema's or a package's defaultStereotypes would give this element, left out with the stereotypes they imply. Only defaults can be excluded (MQ2029).

checks.description: Conditions every record of the entity meets. A database enforces one only through a binding that lists it.

bindings.description: How the entity reads from and writes to databases, one binding per database (erratum E43). A binding wins over any projection of the entity into its database.

items.title: Binding
items.description: How the entity reads from and writes to one database (erratum E43): where it reads, the constant columns, the field map, the columns it accounts for without a field, where it writes back and how it deletes. One per database (MQ4050).

source.description: What the entity reads: the id of a table (or a synthesized table key), a view or a query of the database.

constants.description: Columns with a fixed value: a filter on every read and a value on every insert.

column.description: A column of the source (and of the write table): its key or physical name.

value.description: The value; absent or null is SQL NULL.

fields.description: The field map: an attribute of the entity (attributeId.memberId for a value object member, a relation end id for a to-one navigation's key or, on an end with several types, its id; endId.type for that end's type code and endId.entityId for its key per type) and the source column it reads.

attribute.description: An attribute id of the entity, attributeId.memberId, or the id of a relation end the entity holds, which a to-one navigation leads to: endId maps its key column, or on an end with several types its id column; endId.type maps the column that holds the linked object's type code, and endId.entityId the column that points at a linked object of that entity (a column per type).

column.description: A column of the source: its key or physical name.

columns.description: Source columns no field maps, each accounted for: ignored, filled by the database (never written) or computed.

column.description: A column of the source or the write table: its key or physical name.

write.description: Where the entity writes: { "table": id } or "none". Absent: the source when it is a table, none when it is a view or a query.

table.description: The id of a table of the database (or a synthesized table key).

delete.description: How the entity deletes: "key", { "soft": { "column", "value" } } or "none". Absent: key when the binding writes, none otherwise.

column.description: A column of the write table: its key or physical name.

value.description: The value set; absent or null is SQL NULL.

discriminatorValue.description: The entity's type code in this database, where a type column holds it: a column of a relation end with several types, or the discriminator of an inheritance hierarchy. Absent: the discriminatorValue of the entity's mapping there, else the entity's name. An entity outside a hierarchy takes one only when an end with several types covers it (MQ4009).

provenance.title: Binding provenance
provenance.description: The columns of a table-file source as the last by-name operation (materialize, map-by-name, resync-binding) recorded them, for the drift report and MQ4087. Written by the engine only; a save leaves it as it is, and removing it stops drift reports for the binding. Its keys are records, not references: a column delete never sees them.

columns.description: Column id (an inherited column by its keyed id, <tableId>.<memberId>) to "<name part>:<type part>": two short hashes of the column's name, compared loosely, and of its type, facets and nullability.

checks.description: The ids of the entity's checks the write table enforces, lowered through the field map (MQ3110). A check no binding lists reaches no table.
